steps.title: When to choose CVVH
steps.body: Continuous veno-venous hemofiltration uses convection (replacement fluid) for solute clearance. Best when you need good middle-molecule removal with hemodynamic stability.
steps.tip: Pre-dilution lowers filtration fraction but improves filter life; post-dilution improves clearance efficiency.

steps.title: CVVHD — diffusion dominant
steps.body: Dialysate flows counter-current to blood for small-solute clearance (urea, creatinine, K⁺). Less convection than CVVH; useful when primary goal is small-molecule control.
steps.tip: CVVHD alone may under-clear middle molecules compared with hemofiltration.

steps.title: CVVHDF — combined clearance
steps.body: Adds both replacement fluid (convection) and dialysate (diffusion). Often preferred when maximal solute clearance is needed in ICU AKI.
steps.tip: Total effluent dose still drives overall clearance — target adequate mL/kg/hr.

steps.title: SCUF — ultrafiltration only
steps.body: Slow continuous ultrafiltration without replacement or dialysate. Used primarily for volume removal when solute clearance is not the priority.
steps.tip: Not adequate for severe hyperkalemia or uremia as sole therapy.
